curriculum.lesson_evidence: Tension holds when the key's location stays hidden until the middle. Withhold means you delay a fact the audience wants. The reveal is the moment you finally show it. In the one-minute scene, the audience knows the key is missing and that Riley has chosen to search. They do not yet know where it is. Keep the opening on the empty pocket only. In the middle beat, Alex sees the key ring under the front edge of the paint bench and points, but does not pick it up yet. That is early enough to change the scene and late enough that the audience had to wait. Showing the ring in the first second spends the mystery. Hiding it until the very last second can feel like a trick. The middle is the agreed place for this reveal. Write when the audience first sees the ring. Playing it is optional, with consent and an adult nearby.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
The lost-key scene opens on Riley's empty pocket at the art-room door. When should the audience first see the key ring under the bench?

FEEDBACK
Show the empty pocket first, and keep the bench reveal for the middle beat. The opening withholds the location. The middle shows the ring at the front edge of the paint bench when Alex points. The beginning is too soon, and a last-second surprise is later than this scene needs. The audience should want the location before they receive it.

WATCH FOR
Placing the key in view at the start spends the mystery before it can build. If the ring is already on the bench in the opening picture, there is nothing to withhold. Tension is not the same as shouting or rushing. It is the wait you control. Repair the scene by clearing the key from the opening and letting the point in the middle be the first sight of it.

Hide a library card's location until the middle of a different short scene. The card is missing from a wallet at the loans desk. Do not show where it is in the opening. Write the opening action, the middle reveal, and the reason for waiting. Do not use the house key or the paint bench. Writing is the evidence. Performing needs consent and an adult nearby.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.
